title: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency Anaemias

steps.tx: Impaired nuclear deoxyribonucleic acid synthesis with preserved cytoplasmic ribonucleic acid and protein maturation causes nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony. In **vitamin b12 deficiency** and folate deficiency, diminished intracellular thymidylate production arrests developing erythroblasts in the S-phase of the cell cycle. This leads to marked megaloblastic marrow transformation and accelerated intramedullary destruction of defective erythroid precursors, termed ineffective erythropoiesis. Clinically, patients present with profound weakness, lemon-yellow pallor from combined anaemia and mild indirect hyperbilirubinaemia, atrophic glossitis (Hunter glossitis), and marked peripheral blood macrocytosis with oval macrocytes.
steps.say: Impaired nuclear DNA synthesis with preserved cytoplasmic maturation causes characteristic nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony. In vitamin b12 deficiency and folate deficiency, diminished thymidylate synthesis arrests developing erythroblasts. This produces megaloblastic marrow transformation and accelerated intramedullary destruction of erythroid precursors, termed ineffective erythropoiesis. Patients present with weakness, lemon-yellow pallor, atrophic glossitis, and marked macrocytosis with oval macrocytes.

steps.tx: An autoimmune gastritis targeting gastric oxyntic mucosa destroys acid-secreting parietal cells and intrinsic factor production. As the commonest cause of cobalamin malabsorption, **pernicious anaemia** is mediated by autoantibodies against intrinsic factor (type 1 blocking and type 2 binding antibodies) and gastric H+/K+ ATPase proton pumps. Intrinsic factor antibody testing exhibits over ninety-five percent clinical specificity for pernicious anaemia. Historically, the two-stage radioactive cobalt Schilling test quantified cobalamin absorption before and after intrinsic factor administration, though modern serological assays have supplanted radioactive testing in contemporary practice.
steps.say: An autoimmune gastritis targeting gastric oxyntic mucosa destroys acid-secreting parietal cells and intrinsic factor production. As the commonest cause of cobalamin malabsorption, pernicious anaemia is mediated by autoantibodies against intrinsic factor and gastric parietal cells. Intrinsic factor antibody testing provides high clinical specificity for diagnosis. Historically, the two-stage Schilling test evaluated cobalamin absorption, though modern serological testing has supplanted radioisotope studies.

steps.tx: Examining a stained peripheral blood film provides rapid, definitive morphological confirmation of megaloblastic haematopoiesis. The earliest and most specific peripheral smear hallmark is the presence of **hypersegmented neutrophils**, defined as polymorphonuclear leukocytes possessing six or more distinct nuclear lobes, or more than five percent of neutrophils displaying five lobes. The red blood cells show marked anisopoikilocytosis with characteristic macro-ovalocytes (mean corpuscular volume frequently exceeding 110 to 120 femtolitres), tear-drop poikilocytes, and nucleated red cells with Howell-Jolly bodies reflecting splenic hypofunction.
steps.say: Examining a stained peripheral blood film provides rapid morphological confirmation of megaloblastic haematopoiesis. The earliest and most specific peripheral smear hallmark is the presence of hypersegmented neutrophils, defined by neutrophils possessing six or more nuclear lobes. Red blood cells exhibit marked anisopoikilocytosis with macro-ovalocytes, tear-drop cells, and Howell-Jolly bodies reflecting accelerated, dysplastic marrow output.

steps.tx: Differentiating cobalamin deficiency from folate deficiency requires measuring intermediate metabolic substrates in the methionine and succinyl-CoA cycles. In cobalamin deficiency, both serum **methylmalonic acid** (MMA) and homocysteine concentrations are markedly elevated because vitamin B12 acts as an essential cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase. In contrast, in isolated folate deficiency, homocysteine is elevated but methylmalonic acid remains strictly normal. This biochemical distinction is critical, because treating a B12-deficient patient with folate alone corrects the anaemia while allowing irreversible neurological damage to progress.
steps.say: Differentiating cobalamin deficiency from folate deficiency requires measuring intermediate metabolites in the methionine and succinyl-CoA cycles. In cobalamin deficiency, both serum methylmalonic acid and homocysteine concentrations are markedly elevated because B12 serves as an essential cofactor for mutase and synthase enzymes. In contrast, isolated folate deficiency elevates homocysteine while methylmalonic acid remains strictly normal. Treating B12 deficiency with folate alone corrects anaemia while permitting irreversible neurological degeneration to progress.

steps.tx: Defective myelin methylation in the central nervous system causes progressive axonal demyelination of specific spinal cord white matter tracts. Termed **subacute combined degeneration**, cobalamin deficiency selectively damages the posterior dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts. Patients present symmetrically with lower limb paresthesias, sensory ataxia, loss of vibration and proprioception, positive Romberg sign, and spastic paraparesis with extensor plantar responses (Babinski sign) paired paradoxically with absent ankle jerks due to coexisting peripheral neuropathy. Neuropsychiatric manifestations including dementia, depression, and psychosis (megaloblastic madness) can precede haematological abnormalities.

steps.tx: A common oral biguanide medication interferes with calcium-dependent cobalamin-intrinsic factor complex absorption in the terminal ileum. Developing **metformin-induced b12 deficiency** occurs in up to thirty percent of patients taking long-term metformin therapy, especially at doses exceeding two grams daily for more than three to four years. Metformin impairs membrane charge-dependent calcium uptake required by the cubam receptor complex in the terminal ileal enterocyte brush border. Annual serum B12 monitoring and oral or parenteral replacement therapy prevent misdiagnosing resulting sensory neuropathy as worsening diabetic diabetic neuropathy.

steps.tx: Infection by the longest human intestinal tapeworm acquired through ingestion of raw or undercooked freshwater fish consumes host cobalamin supplies. Designated as **diphyllobothrium latum** (fish tapeworm), this cestode preferentially attaches to the jejunal and ileal mucosa, absorbing up to eighty to one hundred percent of ingested vitamin B12 within the lumen. Heavily infested patients develop overt megaloblastic anaemia with low serum cobalamin levels. Stool examination demonstrates characteristic operculated bile-stained ova, and administration of a single dose of praziquantel achieves complete eradication.

steps.tx: Therapeutic protocols for severe cobalamin deficiency mandate prompt parenteral replacement to arrest irreversible neurological deterioration and replete liver stores. Administering intramuscular **hydroxocobalamin** or cyanocobalamin at one thousand micrograms daily or on alternate days for two weeks, followed by maintenance injections every two to three months, induces rapid reticulocytosis within forty-eight to seventy-two hours. Crucially, clinicians must monitor serum potassium closely during early therapy; rapid massive erythroid blast cell regeneration drives extracellular potassium into newly forming erythrocytes, risking severe, potentially fatal hypokalaemia.
